searchText: Spitballing Engineering question: Would there be advantages to keeping the 2 post-merge clients (~ETH1 + ETH2) as separate and loosely coupled versus merging them together? If kept loosely coupled it seems like this could allow parallel evolution more quickly... At this point in time I think we have this nice separation between the two for most/all clients and perhaps there would be advantages to formalizing that going forward? I guess this would also mean dictating logic flow and separation to clients though... The plan for The Merge is to have them separate. Some people want them to eventually integrate, others want them to remain separate. I'm *weakly* in the "keep them separate" camp, but I can appreciate the arguments made by the opposition. I suspect long term we'll see a mix of both. Nethermind, for example, may end up finishing up Cortex which I believe will be built in to the Nethermind client, while TurboGeth is actively moving toward a service oriented architecture and is very unlikely to integrate the consensus client. It’s very important to note that you don’t need to use separate processes to have a modular client. Besu for example already is very modular with separate teams working on separate components (and plugging in different elements for enterprise networks) but it all runs in a single process. Development modules don’t have to be the same as deployment modules. Call is in 1 hour Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/305 Zoom: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85972471613?pwd=akRKdW1FeWRaWmlNVVc0T1gvUkQvZz09 call in 10 minutes Does the zoom link change each week? there was a mistake last week and two links were in two different places think it's stable now This one is the stable one (I should update my calendar)? yes I still don't understand how the consensus client teams manage to all agree on everything every meeting. At this point, I attend the meetings in hopes of one day discovering the secret. Perhaps the names "consensus client" and "execution client" are more apt than I originally realized... 🤔
